runs.market_commentary:
Asian markets closed mostly higher on Thursday as Japan's Nikkei 225 gained 1.00% to close at 64,594, supported by strength in semiconductor and industrial names following Microsoft's better-than-expected earnings. Samsung Electronics fell roughly 4% in Seoul after reporting a net income miss, and Hang Seng was mixed. The Nikkei's gains were largely driven by global macro optimism and yen weakness ahead of tomorrow's Bank of Japan policy decision, where a hold is the strong consensus.

European markets opened cautiously higher but pared gains as Alphabet's earnings miss began reverberating across the session. The DAX closed up 0.44% to 25,704.02 as German industrials outperformed, while the FTSE 100 barely moved at 10,694.50, up just 0.07%. The ECB is widely expected to hold rates today, but over 80% of market pricing now implies a December hike, keeping pressure on rate-sensitive European equities. Global bond issuance hit a record $6.61 trillion for the year, underscoring continued credit market stress.

US pre-market action on Thursday is dominated by Alphabet's approximately 10% decline after its Q3 earnings report showed slowing search ad revenue and escalating AI infrastructure capex. Nasdaq 100 futures fell roughly 1.2%, while S&P 500 futures slid 0.3–0.4% and Dow futures were mixed. ServiceNow tumbled 18% to $123.27 and Fortinet plunged 25% to $130.15 after both companies delivered disappointing forward guidance. WTI crude is near $102.78 following reports of possible US military action against Iran. Amazon reports Q3 earnings after the bell today, making it the pivotal catalyst for the afternoon session. The Fed held rates at 3.75–4.00% in a 10-2 vote yesterday with Cook and Hammack dissenting for a hike, pushing December hike odds to 83%.

ideas.theme: Big Tech earnings / AWS cloud momentum
ideas.catalyst: Amazon reports Q3 2026 earnings after the bell today, with analysts expecting strong AWS cloud revenue growth and improving retail margins following Microsoft's cloud beat.
ideas.thesis: Amazon's AWS division has been gaining enterprise market share and Microsoft's Azure beat validates the hyperscaler cloud theme heading into today's report; consensus expects roughly 20% AWS growth. A beat and raise could reverse today's tech pessimism and drive a sharp short-squeeze rally in Nasdaq names into the close and through Friday.
ideas.key_risk: If Alphabet's AI infrastructure cost narrative spreads to Amazon's AWS margin outlook, a miss on cloud margins could amplify the current tech selloff.

ideas.theme: AI spending fears / Search revenue deceleration
ideas.catalyst: Alphabet reported Q3 earnings revealing slowing search ad revenue and surging AI infrastructure capex, sending shares down roughly 10% pre-market; Citigroup downgraded to Market Perform.
ideas.thesis: The Alphabet miss reframes investor expectations for the entire Big Tech AI-spend cohort, with the stock breaking below key technical support levels on heavy pre-market volume. Multiple analyst downgrades are likely to follow the session open, and index-fund rebalancing could sustain selling pressure through the week.
ideas.key_risk: An oversold bounce is likely within 48 hours if Amazon beats decisively or if broader market sentiment stabilizes; short-side risk is elevated.

ideas.catalyst: ServiceNow dropped 18% pre-market to approximately $123.27 after guidance disappointed, creating an extreme valuation compression event for one of the highest-quality enterprise SaaS franchises.
ideas.thesis: ServiceNow has historically re-rated higher within weeks of guidance-driven selloffs; at roughly 18x forward revenue post-drop, the stock is approaching its most attractive entry point in two years. Enterprise IT modernization demand remains structurally intact and the guidance conservatism likely reflects Q4 budget digestion, not a fundamental demand shift.
ideas.key_risk: If macro conditions deteriorate or enterprise IT spending further slows, the 18% gap-down may begin a prolonged de-rating rather than a recoverable dip.

ideas.theme: Cybersecurity dip-buy / Fundamental vs. guidance disconnect
ideas.catalyst: Fortinet fell approximately 25% pre-market to $130.15 after forward guidance disappointed, marking one of the largest single-day cybersecurity drawdowns in recent history.
ideas.thesis: Cybersecurity spending is structurally non-discretionary in the current geopolitical environment; a 25% drop on guidance conservatism for a company with double-digit recurring revenue growth creates compelling asymmetric entry. Fortinet's SD-WAN and OS leadership remain intact and peer companies have not pre-announced demand weakness.
ideas.key_risk: The guidance cut may signal a multi-quarter deceleration in product refresh cycles or channel inventory build, which could sustain the selloff beyond an initial bounce.

ideas.catalyst: Trian Fund Management (Nelson Peltz) offered $7.35 per share in cash — a 19% premium — for Wendy's, where Trian already holds a 16.3% stake as the largest shareholder.
ideas.thesis: Activist buyout offers with a 19% premium from an insider holding 16.3% of shares rarely fail; Trian's track record in QSR transactions and the formal disclosed proposal create a hard valuation floor near the bid. Risk/reward strongly favors LONG with a tight stop below the pre-announcement unaffected price.
ideas.key_risk: Board rejection without a higher competing bid or prolonged legal standoff could lock capital in a rangebound stock awaiting deal clarity.

ideas.catalyst: Reuters reports Marvell Technology is in advanced acquisition talks with Lumentum, with a deal announcement potentially as soon as next week to expand Marvell's AI data-center optics portfolio.
ideas.thesis: Lumentum's coherent optics and VCSEL technology are critical enablers of AI data-center interconnects that are supply-constrained; strategic acquirer premiums in this subsector typically run 30-50% above unaffected prices. Advanced-stage talks from a cash-rich acquirer like Marvell significantly increases deal probability and creates a near-term binary upside catalyst.
ideas.key_risk: Talks could break down over valuation disagreements or regulatory review delays, with the stock retracing sharply on any deal collapse or Reuters correction.

ideas.theme: AI memory supercycle / HBM3E pricing power
ideas.catalyst: Micron upgraded to Strong Buy following strong Q4 2026 earnings that confirmed ongoing HBM3E demand and pricing power from AI accelerator customers.
ideas.thesis: Micron is the primary US-listed beneficiary of the HBM memory supercycle; its Q4 beat confirms supply tightness and pricing power for leading-edge memory that shows no signs of abating as AI cluster deployments accelerate. The upgrade cycle from analyst consensus still has upside as HBM3E pricing remains well above commodity DRAM/NAND spot.
ideas.key_risk: A broader Nasdaq selloff driven by AI-spend concerns (as seen with Alphabet today) could drag MU lower in a risk-off tape even as underlying fundamentals remain strong.

ideas.theme: AI infrastructure buildout / Electronic interconnects beat
ideas.catalyst: Amphenol reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS beating estimates by roughly 9.6% with revenue surging 65.1% year over year to $10.23 billion, driven by AI data-center connectivity demand.
ideas.thesis: Amphenol is a best-in-class industrial connector company whose 65% revenue surge reflects the extraordinary AI infrastructure capex cycle; the stock's post-earnings gain of roughly 3.5% appears modest relative to the magnitude of the beat and the revised Street consensus. Multiple upward earnings revisions are likely and the stock typically re-rates into the next quarter after outsized beats.
ideas.key_risk: Broader tech-sector selling from Alphabet and Nasdaq futures weakness today could overwhelm individual stock momentum and limit near-term upside.

ideas.catalyst: Hawaiian Electric upgraded from Strong Sell to Buy as analysts cite improved risk profile, shorter investment horizon post-Maui wildfire normalization, and materially better projected returns.
ideas.thesis: HE has been among the most punished utility stocks of the past two years following the Maui wildfires; the Strong Sell to Buy upgrade from covering analysts indicates the liability overhang is now priced into the stock at current levels. Even with December Fed hike odds at 83%, the magnitude of the re-rating in analyst sentiment creates a compelling asymmetric entry for a dividend-paying utility with improving fundamentals.
ideas.key_risk: Additional wildfire liability claims or adverse regulatory rate case decisions could re-price the stock lower; rising December Fed hike probability is an ongoing headwind for rate-sensitive equities.

deals.headline: Trian Fund Offers $7.35/Share to Take Wendy's Private in 19% Premium Activist Buyout
deals.description: Nelson Peltz's Trian Fund Management, which holds a 16.3% stake in Wendy's as its largest shareholder, submitted a formal cash offer of $7.35 per share representing a 19% premium to the pre-announcement price. The proposal is a take-private attempt that would end Wendy's decades as a public company and mirrors Trian's previous playbook at other consumer brands.

deals.headline: Marvell Technology in Advanced Talks to Acquire Lumentum for Data-Center Optics
deals.description: Reuters reported that Marvell Technology is in advanced acquisition talks with Lumentum Holdings, the coherent optics and VCSEL maker, potentially set to announce a deal as soon as next week. Lumentum's products are critical for high-bandwidth AI data-center interconnects, directly complementing Marvell's custom ASIC and networking chip portfolio.

deals.headline: Scan Global Logistics Acquires US Freight Forwarder OIA Global in Largest-Ever Deal
deals.description: Danish freight forwarder Scan Global Logistics agreed to acquire US-based OIA Global, which generated revenues of $780 million in 2025 and operates across 60 offices with approximately 1,200 employees. The deal is Scan Global's largest single investment and marks a transformational expansion of its North American logistics presence.

deals.headline: MSG Sports Board Approves Spinoff Separating New York Rangers from New York Knicks
deals.description: Madison Square Garden Sports' board of directors formally approved a plan to separate its New York Rangers NHL franchise from its New York Knicks NBA franchise, creating two independently traded public companies. The spinoff is designed to unlock separate valuation multiples for each franchise at a time when professional sports team values have reached record highs globally.

deals.headline: Anthropic Files IPO Prospectus with SEC; Weighs 15-20% Retail Allocation via JPMorgan
deals.description: AI safety company Anthropic filed its long-awaited prospectus with the SEC, setting the stage for one of 2026's highest-profile technology IPOs amid intense institutional demand. Bloomberg reported the company is considering allocating 15-20% of the offering to retail investors and has selected JPMorgan to lead US retail distribution, signaling a broad-based launch strategy.
